# YT Remote 2.0 — mandatory instructions for coding agents and maintainers

**Repository boundary:** Work ONLY in `klckylmz-art/yt-remote-2`. NEVER read, edit, recreate, push, or release `klckylmz-art/yt-remote` (obsolete/deleted). **Desktop only:** native Windows x64 and macOS Intel/Apple Silicon. Do not introduce Android, iOS, HTML frontends, PWA or mobile support.

**Truth and release rule:** The existing source is an UNVERIFIED experimental prototype. A commit, a green compile, or an artifact upload is not proof of an end-to-end working desktop product. Do not call it finished or publish a public stable release unless all mandatory release gates below have evidence. Do not claim physical-device testing you did not perform. Never invent a public relay address, installer, test result, or link. An overnight deadline is an effort priority, not a reason to skip gates.

## Product behavior (non-negotiable)
- English-only, professional native app. Student clicks **GENERATE CODE (STUDENT)** and can **COPY CODE**. Display ONE short copyable code formatted as `XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX`. The teacher pastes/types it and clicks **CONNECT**.
- Student must explicitly press **ALLOW SCREEN & KEYBOARD** for this specific teacher request BEFORE any screen, mouse, or keyboard transmission. Student can press **DENY** or **STOP SHARING NOW**; denial/cancel/end/expiry immediately revoke authorization, stop frames and input, release any pressed keys/buttons. No unattended access; never auto-approve or suppress OS permission prompts.
- The viewer is genuinely fullscreen/borderless and responsive; small top-right **minimize** and **disconnect** controls must be implemented and device-tested. Escape to disconnect is acceptable as a secondary shortcut. No large outer chrome.
- The app, not the person, manages signaling/server addresses. Never ask either user to enter an IP, port, URL or configure an HTTPS proxy. A public host can be configured by the operator/build pipeline, but secrets must not be in repo or distributables.
- Only SCREEN + MOUSE + KEYBOARD. Never add audio/microphone, camera, file transfer, clipboard synchronization, stealth behavior, unattended access, or user tracking. Local copy/paste of a code is permitted.
- Windows 10/11 x64 working .exe or installer; macOS Intel x86_64 and Apple Silicon arm64 working .app and .dmg. macOS screen recording and accessibility grants MUST remain user-controlled. Avoid requiring a paid Apple Developer certificate; unsigned/ad-hoc signed builds need honest Gatekeeper instructions, not security bypass.
- Target 1080p at 60 FPS when measured hardware/network allow, adapt to 30 FPS and lower bandwidth/resolution when needed, prioritize low latency and legible Excel/formula text. No fabricated FPS claims.

## Required implementation order; fix and prove each stage before next

### P0 — Baseline and reproducible CI
1. Inspect existing commits/README, `docs/PLAN.md`, session-core, signaling-server, relay, native GUI, packaging, and `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; capture exact baseline and known blockers. Do not overwrite prior work or ask the user to repeat defined requirements.
2. Confirm repository is public. Standard GitHub-hosted runners are free for public repositories; do not select larger, paid runners or introduce paid external APIs. GitHub runner labels: `ubuntu-latest` for service, `windows-latest` x64, `macos-15` arm64, `macos-15-intel` x64. If Actions refuses to start due to billing/account restriction, report the exact annotation: code edits cannot repair account billing.
3. Make CI validate `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` when feasible, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo build --release -p yt-remote-desktop` on supported OSes. Fix actual error messages, do not assume a 3-second failed workflow means a Rust error. Check packaging output paths and generated artifacts explicitly. Restore code correctness after adding stricter checks.
4. Keep `Cargo.lock` committed, lock dependencies for reproducibility, configure sensible timeouts/cache/artifact retention, and avoid new unneeded CI runs. Prefer coherent small PRs/atomic commits, not hundreds of commits. Never add secrets or .env with credentials.

### P1 — Consent lifecycle, security and native usability
5. Test create/request/allow/deny/cancel/end/expire/replay including race conditions, unauthorized tokens, two teachers racing, code brute-force attempts, network drops, simultaneous stop/frames, stale WS and reconnect. Cancellation MUST invalidate the teacher token and clear the student's pending request; reuse only via a fresh request and explicit new approval. Tests must prove **zero unauthorized frames/input** before approval or after revocation. Rate limit public create/request/status endpoints, cap resource usage, clean up expired sessions and use constant-time comparisons where applicable.
6. Fix native GUI compile/runtime problems, responsive code entry/paste/copy, error recovery, student prompt refresh, window ownership, font scaling/HiDPI, focus handling, meaningful connection states. UI must remain responsive during slow HTTP/TLS/WS calls (bounded I/O + worker thread/event state). Do not rely on indefinite synchronous network calls on the UI loop.
7. Implement proper screen capture OS permission handling (macOS Screen Recording; Accessibility for input; Windows capture APIs/permissions). Handle multiple screens, correct source monitor selection, mouse coordinate transforms with letterboxing/Retina/scaling, and keyboard modifiers/layouts. Always release held keys and mouse buttons after disconnect.
8. Keep HTTPS/WSS authenticated transport for all non-loopback communication. Validate endpoints and certificates; never disable TLS verification. Prevent anonymous WebSocket upgrades, session hijacking, ID guessing, auth-token leakage, SSRF/cross-origin abuse and unbounded queues. If media is visible to the relay, be transparent; end-to-end encryption is a goal and a release blocker if security claims require it. Do not claim E2EE without verified implementation/tests. No audio/files/clipboard paths.

### P2 — Working internet transport and measured video
9. Choose and implement a realistic, reviewed path: reliable secure relay with optional P2P/direct path + fallback. Do NOT claim to have P2P merely because a WebSocket relay exists. A real host, TLS hostname, credentials and DNS require an authorized operator; do not invent credentials or charge the user. Keep private deployment configs/keys out of public GitHub. Add deployment IaC/container/docs, health checks, rate limits, logs without secrets, resource bounds, graceful restarts.
10. Implement efficient capture/encoding/decoding or transport suitable for a real remote desktop, with hardware acceleration when supported and safe fallback. Avoid continuous full-frame JPEG at fixed 1280x720 as a final solution. Add adaptive bitrate/resolution/FPS logic, a bounded last-frame-wins queue, jitter/RTT instrumentation and recovery. Test real 1920x1080 Excel text and estimate latency from actual measurements. If hardware path cannot be finished, leave it explicitly incomplete and keep the app experimental.
11. Test separate-network student/teacher through the deployed HTTPS/WSS endpoint, restrictive NAT/firewall, reconnect, packet loss, high latency, relay restart and user STOP. Authentication and consent MUST survive neither unintended reconnection nor old-token reuse.

### P3 — Packaging, smoke tests and release
12. Produce Windows x64 native executable and a usable installation method; package macOS x86_64 + arm64 .app/.dmg with correct architecture, Info.plist, icon, bundle IDs and ad-hoc signatures if needed. Verify actual binary architecture and executable is included; validate installers on clean OS installations. If a public server endpoint is not deployed, never present a localhost-configured binary as a working zero-configuration internet app.
13. Add transport integration tests that run against a real local server, and manual physical-device checklists covering Windows↔Windows, Windows↔macOS, macOS↔Windows, Intel↔Apple Silicon if devices are available; consent denied, cancel, stop, network failure, wrong codes, 1080p Excel readability, top-right minimize/exit, high DPI, multi-display.
14. Provide evidence for each OS: green CI build/check/test logs, downloadable install artifacts, packaging/signing verification, real installation/screen-grant screenshots or logs, real two-computer cross-network test evidence, benchmark results with achieved FPS/latency, SHA256 checksums and accurate known limitations. Only THEN tag/publish a GitHub release. Without physical machines or a deployable relay, record a blocker and deliver verified prototype artifacts only, marked UNTESTED/EXPERIMENTAL.
15. Document installation, explicit permission steps, immediate STOP behavior, troubleshooting, privacy, server ops and licenses of third-party components. Do not bypass OS security controls or require paid signing.

## Continuous implementation rules
- On EACH iteration, inspect the current branch, choose the highest-severity unblocked item, implement a concrete safe change, add/update tests, review diff, and verify locally where possible. Check GitHub Actions actual logs before asserting a fix works.
- Work in coherent batches/PRs; do not race other agents or clobber newer commits. If main advanced, fetch and rebase/merge carefully. Treat failing checks as blockers, not as justification to delete tests or weaken security.
- Never fabricate success. Report (a) exact change and commit/PR, (b) command/CI tested and its result, (c) what remains and why, (d) anything requiring external credentials, physical device or explicit operator action.
- Focus work toward the next morning, but never declare completion just because of the clock. No user notification claiming release unless all actual gates pass. Continue with highest-value remaining tasks if safe.
